title: Chinese observations of the supernova of 1054 (Crab Nebula)
summary: Astronomers at the Song court in China recorded a guest star near Tianguan that first appeared on 4 July 1054, was seen in daylight for 23 days, and faded after more than a year. Japanese records also mention it. Modern astronomers identify it as the supernova that left the Crab Nebula, about 6,500 light-years away.

uncertainty.note: Start is the date of the first Song record. End of visibility is given only as "a year and more" in the Song shi (1055 to 1056); the 1056 end year is an approximation.

as_recorded.value: In 1054, Chinese astronomers took notice of a "guest star"

where.historical_name: Kaifeng, capital of the Song dynasty

importance.justification: One of the best-documented historical supernovae, whose remnant was later identified as the Crab Nebula.

sources.title: Notes on translations of the East Asian records relating to the supernova of AD 1054 (Journal of Astronomical History and Heritage 9(1))

reviewer_note: Least sure of the pin: Pankenier gives the Song capital at Kaifeng as 34.47 N, 114.20 E, while Wikidata gives 34.795 N, 114.345 E; the 40 km uncertainty covers both. The Song huiyao astrological report dated to late August 1054 is a separate record and is not used for the start date. The end year is approximate.
